newsitem.title: EGYPT: PRESS DIGEST - Egypt economic press - Feb 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Egypt economic press - Feb 2.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian economic press this week. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Lack of new listings contributes to price surge on the Egyptian bourse and brokers expect the uptrend to continue as demand remains high.

- The government's privatisation committee decides this week to sell share tranches in several firms by the first quarter of the year. These include 30 percent of Paints and Chemical Industries/Pachin, five to 10 percent of Heliopolis Housing and Development, five percent of Arab Cotton Ginning, 10 percent of Alexandria Cotton Ginning, Kabo/Nasr Clothing and Textiles and Extracted Oils and Derivatives, 20 percent of Eastern Company and Eipico/Egyptian International Pharmaceutical Industries. State will also totally privatise firms in which it has sold more than 51 percent excluding the cement firms.
- National Bank of Egypt raising capital for its two mutual funds by 100 million pounds each.
- Capital Markets Authority grants the National Bank of Egypt and 20 other companies book-keeping rights.

- East Delta Flour Mills increases pretax profits for the first half of 1996/7 financial year to 20.5 million pounds from 16.19 million in the same period in the previous year. The increase is due to the restructuring of the company's labour and streamlining its pasta manufacturing unit. The financial year ends on June 30.

- Central and West Delta Flour Mills raises after-tax profits for the first six months of 1996/7 to 35.317 million from 23.568 million in the same year ago period. Sales also rose to 298.612 million from 249.401 million.
- North Cairo Flour Mills profits down for the six months ending December 1996 to 14.9 million from 15.1 million in the same period of the previous year.
- Unaudited profits for Misr International Bank/MIBANK for calendar 1996 show that profits rose to 141.2 million from 95.7 million in the previous year.
- Commercial International Bank decides to issue bonds worth 900 million pounds.
- State offers a minimum 1.2 million shares in Nile Cotton Ginning at 40 pounds a share.
